body.prompt:
Use case: ChandRush Chapter 02 location reference plate L02_C, a medium three-quarter view of the cool filling area on the Food Street cooking counter, used in a fractions scene (adding 1¾ kg and 2½ kg and sharing into five trays), so the labels and the tray count must be exact.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image of an empty location, no characters.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved working view of this same counter. Use it for: the counter, the covered brass filling bowls, the sharing trays, the recipe end (book, balance) and the dispenser design (tank on legs, hinged cup) where they appear at the edges; materials and light. Ignore: anything outside this closer view.
- Image 2: the approved Food Street master. Use it for: finish and lamps. Ignore: all white label boxes, annotation words and arrows; cart, bowls on the floor, trolley, table.
Camera and framing: medium three-quarter view from the customer aisle, standing eye height, looking down at about 35 degrees onto the filling area. Frame-left: the recipe book and two-pan balance at the dry entrance end, partly cut by the edge. Frame-right: the brass base and support legs of the empty dispenser tank and the empty hinged cup, cut by the edge. The pale slab front edge crosses the lower third; blue cupboard fronts below; timber backdrop above.
Place and construction, back to front on the filling area:
1. Back row: exactly 2 (two) covered round brass filling bowls with domed lids, side by side, separate. Each has a cream card label plate fixed on its front, about one twelfth of the frame width.
2. Middle: one larger empty open brass mixing bowl, its inside visibly empty, with a blank cream label plate on its front (nothing written).
3. Front row: exactly 5 (five) shallow round empty brass sharing trays in one straight row along the front edge, with clear gaps, separate, none stacked or overlapping. Five in total.
4. Towards frame-right, clear of the other vessels: one small empty trial bowl.
5. Every vessel rests flat on the slab.
State at this moment (exact): both filling bowls covered; mixing bowl empty; all 5 (five) trays empty; trial bowl empty; dispenser tank and cup empty, supply tap closed; heater off.
Physical inscriptions (render exactly, nothing else): "1¾ kg" in large bold dark numerals on the left covered bowl's label; "2½ kg" in large bold dark numerals on the right covered bowl's label. Fractions with a clean bar. The mixing bowl's label is blank. The recipe book page, if visible, shows "1¾ kg". No other numbers, letters or words anywhere.
Keep clear and visible: the front edge opposite the two covered bowls; the slab beside the mixing bowl's near rim; the front edge beside the tray row; both labels, the empty mixing bowl and all five tray outlines.
Light: fixed amber work lamp, cool moonlight on brass.
Do not show: a sixth tray or only four; trays stacked; filling in any vessel; writing on the mixing bowl label; any person, hand or animal; label boxes or arrows.

Look and finish (same for every ChandRush location plate): premium semi-realistic painterly 2.5D graphic-novel illustration that matches the supplied ChandRush masters, a blend of illustration and reality. It is painterly in finish but crisp and precise in drawing. Materials and light have near-photographic conviction while forms stay clean, idealised and orderly, like a high-end storybook. ChandRush is an ancient travelling fair with grand, mystic, magical scale and real architectural detailing: dimensional deep-indigo and ultramarine painted timber with visible grain, joinery, rivets and edge banding; warm polished and cast brass with bright specular edges and a light patina; pale cream stone worktops and pale irregular stone paving with a light wet sheen and crisp reflections; layered fabric canopies; restrained circular celestial ornament (full-moon discs, rings, small eight-point stars) in gold and brass. Palette: ultramarine, cobalt, indigo and navy against amber, honey-gold and brass, with strong warm-cool contrast, saturated but natural, never neon. Light: fixed amber task lamps cast clean, well-defined warm pools, their glow held tight around the lamp glass with no spreading halo; cool full-moon light edges roofs, canopy gaps, stone and brass; deep, rich shadows that keep readable detail. Clarity: clear, dry night air with no haze, fog, mist, smoke or airborne dust. Crisp edges and high micro-contrast. Sharp, clean textures in wood grain, brass and stone, as in a high-resolution photograph. True deep darks and clean colours, never a milky, washed-out or glowing veil over the image, never soft focus. The background stays crisp and only slightly darker with distance. Ornament is dense above eye level and on frames; floors, worktops and mechanisms stay open, clean and readable.

Production rules (apply to every plate):
- Frame: one 4:3 landscape scenic image filling the whole canvas edge to edge. No border, title band, panel frame, vignette box or blank margin.
- Lettering: the only lettering allowed is the physical inscriptions listed above, rendered exactly as written, letter for letter, with each minus sign as a true minus sign. No other words, numbers or symbols anywhere. No title, caption, callout, label box, leader line, arrow, legend, watermark or signature: titles and callouts are added later by the production team.
- Reference images: their titles, annotation words, label boxes and arrows only identify places for you. Reproduce none of them.
- Empty location: no people, children, helpers, wooden figures, animals, hands, shadows of figures or silhouettes. The place waits, ready for characters to be added later.
- Counts and states are exact as stated. Add no extra copies of any counted object and no extra devices, cards, lamps or tiles.
- Unlit means unlit: clear or smoky glass with no flame, no inner glow and no bloom. Lit lamps glow only at their own glass.
- Avoid: haze, fog, mist, bloom halos, soft focus, a low-contrast or milky wash, modern signage, plastic, neon, sci-fi screens, crowds, text on fabric or banners, mirrored or garbled lettering, duplicated objects, warped or melted geometry, a second moon in the sky, a crescent moon.

Use case: ChandRush Chapter 02 location reference plate L02_D, a medium three-quarter view of the Food Street dosa dispenser and its controls before the portion stop is adjusted. Later views (cold test and corrected serving) reuse this exact camera and dispenser.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image of an empty location, no characters.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved working view of this same cooking counter. Use it for: the exact dispenser design (one brass tank on fixed legs with its narrow inspection window, supply tap, the single hinged measuring cup with its scale strip, tick marks and sliding fill stop, the long wood-gripped handle, the guarded iron cooking plate, the heater switch, the dry plate shelf), the two dosas and their plates, materials and light. Keep every fitting's shape identical. Ignore: the far-left recipe end and filling area (mostly out of frame here).
- Image 2: the approved Food Street master. Use it for: overall finish, materials and lamps. Ignore: all white label boxes, annotation words and arrows; cart, bowls, trolley, table.
Camera and framing: medium three-quarter view from the cool customer side of the counter, standing eye height, looking slightly down and towards frame-right. The entrance end is frame-left. The whole dispenser fills the centre: tank top near the top edge, the full long handle, the measuring cup, the guarded cooking plate behind, and the dry plate shelf at frame-right all fit within the frame. The cream front slab edge crosses the lower third; the indigo timber joint of the backdrop and the tank's support legs are visible. The supply tap grip and handle grip face the camera across the cool front edge; the hot plate lies farther back behind its guard. A clear strip of paving shows at the bottom.
Place and construction: exactly as in Image 1. One brass tank on fixed legs; narrow glass inspection window on its lower front-left; supply tap below with its grip towards frame-left and the viewer; one measuring cup under the spout, hinge on its right side fixed to the support leg, wooden-grip bracket on its left; a vertical brass scale strip inside the cup's front wall with exactly 3 (three) unlabelled tick marks and a sliding brass fill-stop clip; long handle with dark wooden grip reaching towards the front edge; black iron cooking plate behind a low brass guard rail with a small rotary heater switch; a raised cream dry plate shelf at frame-right outside the guard.
State at this moment (exact):
1. Tank empty, inspection window shows empty interior.
2. Supply tap OPEN: its lever turned in line with the spout (no batter flows because the tank is empty).
3. Measuring cup empty; seated under the spout; fill stop fixed just above the lowest unlabelled tick.
4. Long handle raised at rest; cup bottom outlet closed.
5. Cooking plate empty; heater switch turned to ON, a small amber jewel lamp beside the switch lit; the plate surface shows a faint dull heat shimmer only, no flames, no steam.
6. Dry shelf: exactly 2 (two) separate small white plates: one holds the oversized golden dosa overhanging its rim; the other holds the tiny dosa. No other plates.
7. The foreground paving strip and both grips are clear.
Physical inscriptions (render exactly, nothing else): none. No numbers, letters or words anywhere; the tick marks are unlabelled.
Keep clear and visible: paving in front of the long handle; the supply-tap grip; the cup's fill stop and lowest tick; the rear working aisle beside the cooking plate at frame-right.
Light: fixed amber work lamp above, cool moonlight on brass.
Do not show: batter anywhere; flames; a second cup or tank; numbers on the cup scale; a third plate; any person, hand or animal; label boxes or arrows.

Use case: ChandRush Chapter 02 location reference plate L02_G, a low three-quarter view along the dry plate shelf of the Food Street cooking counter, showing the oversized and the tiny cooked dosas at a child's eye level.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image of an empty location, no characters.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved working view of this same counter. Use it for: the dry plate shelf, the two plates and dosas, and the exact dispenser design (tank on fixed legs with narrow inspection window, supply tap, one hinged measuring cup with its tick strip and fill stop, long wood-gripped handle, guarded iron plate); cupboard base, materials and light.
- Image 2: the approved Food Street master. Use it for: finish, paving and lamps. Ignore: all white label boxes, annotation words and arrows; cart, floor bowls, trolley, table.
Camera and framing: low three-quarter view from the customer aisle, camera just above the shelf surface, looking along the shelf towards frame-right and tilted gently down. The entrance end is frame-left. The shelf's cream front lip crosses the middle of the frame; the indigo shelf supports and cupboard base are below it; clear pale paving fills the bottom third. The lower part of the brass dispenser (tank legs, cup, handle, guard) is visible behind and above the shelf.
State at this moment (exact):
1. On the shelf exactly 2 (two) small round white plates, side by side, separate, resting fully on the shelf. Left plate: one oversized golden cooked dosa, much wider than its plate, overhanging the rim all round. Right plate: one tiny cooked dosa covering only the centre of its plate. Both dosa tops visible.
2. Tank and cup empty; fill stop above the lowest unlabelled tick; supply tap closed; long handle raised.
3. The paving below the shelf and in front is clear, with two separate open patches; the cool front lip is clear.
Physical inscriptions (render exactly, nothing else): none. No numbers, letters or words anywhere.
Keep clear and visible: both dosa sizes and their shelf contact; the paving below the shelf away from the legs; a separate clear floor patch to its left; the front lip above that patch.
Light: warm task light across shelf and floor; cool moonlight on brass.
Do not show: a third plate; dosas off the shelf; batter; any person, hand or animal; label boxes or arrows.
